title: Camden and southern New Jersey
summary: Camden had little to offer a big band; trains ran straight to Atlantic City.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: How about some of the places in-between, Teddy? For example, Camden, New Jersey. Did Charlie Johnson's band or even the McRae Brothers' band play in Camden?
We never played in Camden. Camden was a place that never had too much to offer to a big band.
Years ago, we used to play a dance there
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
or something. Camden was like a stopover, you know.
Some of these little towns in southern New Jersey?
Yeah. Camden was never -- You know, Jersey was just being built up. Go and take the train, you go straight to Atlantic City. You ride a train down to Atlantic City.
